newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire talks to be held on Friday - Mandela office.
newsitem.headline: Zaire talks to be held on Friday - Mandela office.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said through a spokesman on Thursday that he would chair face-to-face talks between President Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire and rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Friday aboard a South African naval vessel off the coast of west Africa.
"Tomorrow the two groups will meet on the ship. The discussions will take place tomorrow," Mandela's spokesman Parks Mankahlana told Reuters in Cape Town.

He said Mandela would escort Mobutu to the ship from Pointe Noire, on the coast of Congo, and South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki would accompany Kabila to the vessel from Luanda, the Angola capital.
U.S. envoy Bill Richardson, who earlier announced the date and venue for the encounter, was expected in Luanda on Thursday afternoon.
Earlier on Thursday, Mobutu's camp said they understood the meeting was being postponed for a day until Saturday.
